(p-219) Surah As-Sajdah is Meccan, and its number of verses is thirty, though it is said to be twenty-nine.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim.﴾ If it is taken as the name of the surah or of the Qur'an, then it is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is:

﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, on the basis that tanzil (revelation) is in the sense of the munazzal (that which is sent down). If it is taken as an enumeration of the letters, then ﴿tanzil﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, or a subject whose predicate is: ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾, in which case ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in ﴿in it﴾, because the verbal noun (masdar) does not govern what comes after the predicate. It is also permissible that it be a second predicate, and that ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ be a circumstantial clause (hal) from ﴿the Book﴾, or a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD), with the pronoun in it referring to the content of the sentence. This is supported by His saying:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ For this is a denial that it is from the Lord of the worlds, and His saying: ﴿Rather, it is the truth from your Lord﴾ is an affirmation of it. The arrangement of the discourse on this basis is that He first pointed to its inimitability (i'jaz), then ordered upon it that its revelation is from the Lord of the worlds, and confirmed that by negating doubt about it. Then He turned away from that to what they say about it, contrary to that, as a denial of it and an expression of wonder at it. For ﴿am﴾ here is disjunctive (munqati'ah). Then He turned away from it to affirm that it is the truth sent down from Allah, and He clarified the purpose of its revelation, saying: ﴿That you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾, since they were a people of the interval (ahl al-fatrah) [between prophets], ﴿so that they may be guided﴾ by your warning them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 4:

﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He established Himself upon the Throne.﴾ Its explanation has passed in "al-A'raf" (the seventh surah). ﴿You have no guardian or intercessor besides Him.﴾

(﴿You have no…﴾) If you transgress Allah's pleasure, there is no one who will help you or intercede for you; or the meaning is: you have no guardian or intercessor other than Him, rather He is the One who takes charge of your affairs and helps you in the situations where you need help. The intercessor (shafi') is here used figuratively for the helper (nasir), so that if He forsakes you, you will have no guardian and no helper left. ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ by the admonitions of Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 5–6:

﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth.﴾ He manages the affairs of the world through heavenly means, such as the angels and others, whose effects descend to the earth. ﴿Then it ascends to Him.﴾ Then it rises to Him and becomes established in His knowledge as something existing. ﴿In a Day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count.﴾ In a span of time that is extended, meaning the length of time between the arranging and the occurrence. It was also said: He arranges the affair by making it manifest in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh), and the angel descends with it, then it ascends to Him in a time equal to a thousand years, because the distance of its descent and ascent is a journey of a thousand years, since the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years. (p-220)

It was also said: He decrees a decree of a thousand years, so the angel descends with it, then it ascends after the thousand years for another thousand. It was also said: He arranges the affair until the Hour is established, then the whole affair ascends to Him on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: He arranges what is commanded of acts of obedience, sent down from the heaven to the earth through revelation, and then it does not ascend to Him purified as He is pleased with, except after a lengthy period, because of the scarcity of the sincere and of purely sincere deeds. It was also recited as «يَعْرُجُ» (yaʿruju, "it ascends," a reading in which the verb is in the singular) and «يَعْدُونَ» (yaʿudūna, "they count," a reading in which the verb is in the plural, addressed to the people who count).

﴿That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.﴾ So He arranges their affair in accordance with wisdom. ﴿The Mighty⦆ the Victorious over His affair. ﴿The Merciful⦆ toward the servants in His management, and in this there is an indication that He takes account of the interests out of bounty and benevolence.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 7–9:

﴿Who made everything He created most good﴾, giving it a creation in which He bestowed upon it all that it is prepared for and fitting for it, in accordance with wisdom and benefit. "Khalaqahu" (He created it) is a substitute for "kulla" (everything), a substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal). And "qala" (He knew) comes from their saying: "qimat al-mar' ma yuhsinuhu", meaning the worth of a person is what he knows well, i.e., his knowledge of it is good; and "khalaqahu" is the second object. Nafi' and the Kufans read "lamm" with a fatha (as "khalaqahu") as a description (wasf); so "shay'" (thing) according to the first reading is specified by a disjunct (munfasil), and according to the second by a conjunct (muttasil).

﴿And He began the creation of man﴾, meaning Adam, ﴿from clay﴾.

﴿Then He made his offspring﴾, his progeny, so named because they issue forth (tansull) from him, i.e., separate, ﴿from an extract of a base fluid﴾, i.e., despised (mumtahan).

﴿Then He fashioned him﴾, straightened him, by shaping his limbs as is fitting. ﴿And breathed into him of His spirit﴾, an attribution to Himself as an honour for him and an indication that he is a wondrous creation, and that he has a station having some affinity to the Lordly presence. For this reason it was said: "Whoever knows himself, knows his Lord." ﴿And He made for you hearing and sight and hearts﴾, specifically so that you might hear, see and understand. ﴿Little are you grateful﴾, meaning you give little thanks.

And they say, ﴿"When we have gone astray in the earth?"﴾ That is, we have become dust mixed with the dust of the earth, so that we cannot be distinguished from it; or, we have disappeared into it.

It is recited as ﴿ḍalil-nā﴾ with a kasra, from ḍalla yaḍillu (to go astray), and as ﴿waṣalal-nā﴾ from ṣalla al-laḥmu (the flesh became putrid) when it rots. Ibn ʿĀmir reads ﴿idhā﴾ as a statement (khabar), and its governing element (ʿāmil) is what the preceding phrase implies. ﴿"Shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ That is: we will be raised, or our creation will be renewed. Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read ﴿annā﴾ as a statement, and the speaker was Ubayy ibn Khalaf. The attribution is made to all of them because they approved of it. ﴿"Nay, but they are in disbelief of the meeting with their Lord"﴾: meaning the resurrection, or the encounter with the angel of death and what follows it. ﴿Kāfirūn﴾ means those who deny and reject.

﴿Say: "The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you up"﴾: yatawaffā means he fully takes your souls, leaving nothing of them and sparing none of you. The form tafaʿʿala (tawaffā) and the form istafʿala (istawfā) often coincide in meaning, as in taqaṣṣaytuhu and istaqṣaytuhu (I investigated it thoroughly) and taʿajjaltuhu and istaʿjaltuhu (I hastened it). ﴿The angel of death who has been entrusted with you﴾ means entrusted with seizing your souls and counting your appointed terms. ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ for reckoning and recompense.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 12:

﴿And if only you could see when the guilty will hang their heads before their Lord﴾ from shame and disgrace. ﴿"Our Lord"﴾ saying, "Our Lord." ﴿"We have seen"﴾ what You promised us. ﴿"and we have heard"﴾ from You the confirmation of Your messengers. ﴿"So return us"﴾ to the world. ﴿"that we may do righteousness. Indeed, we are certain"﴾ since no doubt remains for us about what we have witnessed. (p-221)

As for the answer to "law" (law, "if"), it is omitted, its estimated meaning being: "you would see a dreadful matter." It is permissible that it be for wishing (tamanni) and that the past tense in it and in "idh" (when) is used, because what is fixed in the knowledge of God is in the position of what has occurred. No object is estimated for "tara" (you see), because the meaning is: "if there were a seeing from you at this time." Or what the relative clause of "idh" indicates is estimated. The address is to the Messenger ﷺ or to every person.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 13–14:

﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾: that is, its guidance to faith and righteous action, by granting it success (tawfiq) in that.

﴿But the word from Me has been fulfilled﴾: that is, My decree has been established and My threat has preceded, and it is: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together﴾. This is an explicit statement that they will not believe, due to the absence of [divine] will, which is caused by the prior judgment that they are among the people of the Fire. And it is not refuted by making the tasting of the punishment caused by their forgetting the outcome and their not reflecting upon it, in His saying:

﴿So taste [it] for having forgotten the meeting of this your Day﴾. For this is among the intermediaries and causes that necessitate it.

﴿Indeed, We have forgotten you﴾: We have abandoned you from mercy; or, in punishment, [it is] the abandonment of one who is forgotten. The resumption of the statement and the construction of the verb with "inna" and its noun indicates emphasis in retribution against them.

﴿And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do﴾. He repeated the command for emphasis, and because of what is attached to it of explicitly mentioning its object, and because He gave as its cause their evil deeds, such as denial and disobedience, just as He gave as its cause their neglect of contemplating the outcome and reflecting upon it. This indicates that each of these two requires that [punishment].

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 15–16:

﴿Indeed, those who believe in Our signs are only those who, when they are reminded of them,﴾ are admonished by them. ﴿fall down in prostration﴾ out of fear of the punishment of Allah. ﴿and glorify [their Lord]﴾ they declare Him far above what does not befit Him, such as incapacity to resurrect. ﴿with praise of their Lord﴾ giving thanks to Him, praising Him for having guided them to Islam and granted them guidance. ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾ against faith and obedience, unlike one who persists in arrogance.

﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ they rise up and withdraw from the couches, the spreads, and the places of sleep. ﴿calling upon their Lord﴾ invoking Him, ﴿in fear﴾ of His wrath, and ﴿in hope﴾ of His mercy.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning its interpretation: "The standing of the servant in the night [in prayer]."

And from him, upon him be blessings and peace: "When Allah gathers the first and the last in one plain, a caller will call out with a voice that makes all creatures hear: 'The people of the gathering will know today who is most deserving of honour.' Then he returns and calls: 'Let those stand whose sides used to forsake their beds.' They stand, and they are few. Then he returns and calls: 'Let those stand who used to praise Allah in ease and in hardship.' They stand, and they are few. Then they all are sent off to Paradise, and then the rest of the people are called to account."

It was also said that some of the Companions used to pray between Maghrib and 'Isha, and this verse was revealed concerning them. ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ in the ways of good.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 17:

﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them﴾ — neither a closely-brought angel nor a sent prophet. ﴿of comfort for the eyes﴾ — that which their eyes find delight in.

And from him (ﷺ), upon him be prayers and peace, [it is related]: "Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to the heart of any human being, let alone what I have shown them of it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿So no soul knows what is hidden for them﴾."

Hamzah and Ya'qub read ﴿ukhfiya lahum﴾ as a present-tense verb (mudari') of akhfaytu [i.e., "ukhfī", "I hide"], and it has also been read as "nukhfī" and "ukhfī"; the agent in all of them is Allah. "And eyes [of various kinds] recited" (p-222) — because their kinds differ. The verb 'alima (to know) is here in the sense of ma'rifah (recognition, knowing), and "mā" is either a relative pronoun (mawsulah) or an interrogative (istifhamiyyah) whose verb is suspended (mu'allaq) from taking effect on it.

﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ — that is, "Be rewarded with a reward," or "It is hidden for the reward," for its concealment is due to the greatness of its status. It has also been said that this refers to a people who concealed their deeds, so Allah concealed their reward.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 18–19:

﴿Is then he who is a believer like him who is a defiant sinner (fāsiq)?﴾ (i.e., one who has departed from faith) ﴿They are not equal﴾ in honour and reward. This is emphasis and clarification, and the plural (lā yastawūn) is used to convey the meaning (al-ḥaml ʿalā al-maʿnā), since "man" (man) is grammatically singular but semantically plural.

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens of refuge (jannāt al-ma'wā)﴾ For indeed they are the true refuge, and this world is a station from which one must inevitably depart. It was also said that al-ma'wā is a garden among the gardens. ﴿As a welcome (nuzul)﴾ This term was discussed in Surat Āl ʿImrān. ﴿For what they used to do﴾ i.e., because of their deeds, or in recompense for their deeds.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 20–21:

﴿As for those who defied (fasaqu), their refuge is the Fire﴾ — in place of the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa) for the believers. ﴿Whenever they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾ — an expression for their remaining in it forever. ﴿And it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny"﴾ — as humiliation for them and an increase in their rage.

﴿And We will surely make them taste of the nearer punishment﴾ — the punishment of this world, meaning what they were tried with of the famine for seven years, and of killing and captivity.

﴿Short of the greater punishment﴾ — the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿That perhaps they may return﴾ — that perhaps those among them who remain may repent of disbelief. It is narrated that al-Walid ibn 'Uqba boasted against 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) on the day of Badr, and then these verses were revealed.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 22–24:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them?﴾ Then he did not reflect upon them. The word ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ (thumma, "then") here indicates that turning away from them is strange, given how plainly clear they are and how they guide to the means of happiness after being brought to mind through reason. This is like the line in the Hamasa (the anthology of Abu Tammam, a collection of early Arabic poetry): "None removes the distress except the son of a free woman, who sees the throes of death and then visits them."

﴿Indeed, We will take vengeance upon the criminals.﴾ So how much more so upon one who was more unjust than every wrongdoer?

﴿And We gave Musa the Book﴾ as We gave you (the Book). ﴿So do not be in doubt﴾ ﴿about his meeting﴾: about your meeting with the Book, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed you receive the Qur'an﴾. We gave you of the Book the like of what We gave him, so that is no novelty that never existed before, such that you should doubt it. Or (the meaning is) about Musa's meeting with the Book, or about your meeting with Musa.

It is also related from him (ﷺ) (i.e., the Prophet), upon whom be prayers and peace: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw Musa (ﷺ), a man of brown complexion, tall, with curly hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah."

﴿And We made it﴾ — that is, what was revealed to Musa — ﴿a guidance for the Children of Israel.﴾ (p-223)

﴿And We made from among them leaders who guide﴾ people to what it contains of wisdom and rulings, ﴿by Our command﴾, meaning by Our command to them to do so, or by Our enabling them to do so.

﴿When they were patient﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ruways read ﴿lamma sabaru﴾ (with the verb in the form that yields "when they had been patient"); the meaning is: because of their patience in obedience or in abstaining from the world. ﴿And they were certain of Our signs﴾, because they looked into them with careful contemplation.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 25–26:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the One who will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ He decides, and thereby distinguishes the truth from falsehood by distinguishing the one who is right (al-muhiqq) from the one who is wrong (al-mubtil). ﴿Concerning that in which they used to differ﴾ regarding matters of the religion.

﴿Did it not guide them?﴾ The waw (wa) is a conjunction (ʿatf) on an implied clause of the same kind as the conjoined clause, and the subject (fa'il) is a pronoun referring to what is indicated by that implied clause. ﴿How many generations before them did We destroy?﴾ That is, the number of generations of the past that We destroyed; or the pronoun refers to God, as is shown by the reading with the nun (we, "Nahlik").

﴿They walk through their dwellings﴾ meaning the people of Makkah pass by their ruins (diyar) while going to their trading places (matajir). It was also read as "yumashshun" with the doubled shin (causative/intensive form). ﴿Indeed, in that are signs. Will they not hear?﴾ meaning hearing with reflection and taking admonition.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 27:

﴿Do they not see that We drive the water to the barren land?﴾ The barren land (al-ardh al-juruz) is the one whose vegetation has been cut off and removed (juriza nabatuha, ay qutiʿa wa-uzila), not the land that does not produce plants at all, as indicated by His words:

﴿So We bring forth thereby crops﴾. It is also said that al-Juruz is the name of a place in Yemen.

﴿From which their livestock eat﴾, namely from the crops, ﴿such as fodder and leaves﴾ (al-tin wa-al-waraq).

﴿And themselves﴾, such as grain and fruit (al-habb wa-al-thamar). ﴿Will they not then see?﴾ So that they may reflect upon it and infer from it the perfection of His power and His bounty.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 28–29:

﴿And they say, "When is this victory?"﴾ The victory (al-nasr) or the decisive judgment (al-fasl bi'l-hukumah), from His saying ﴿"Our Lord, decide between us"﴾, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in the promise of it.

﴿Say, "On the Day of Victory, their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved, nor will they be reprieved."﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, for it is the Day of the victory of the believers over the disbelievers and of the decisive judgment between them. It was also said that it is the Day of Badr, or the Day of the Conquest of Mecca (Fath Makkah), and what is meant by "those who disbelieved" are those among them who were killed on it, for their faith will not benefit them at the moment of killing, and they will not be given respite. Its fit as an answer to their question is in terms of meaning, in view of what is known of their purpose: since they intended by it hasty demand, as denial and mockery, they were answered with what prevents hastiness.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 30:

﴿So turn away from them﴾, and do not care about their denial. It has also been said that it is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword. ﴿And wait﴾ for victory over them. ﴿Indeed they too are waiting﴾ for victory over you. It is also read with a fatha (فتح) on the inna, in the sense that they deserve to have their destruction awaited, or that the angels are waiting for it.

From the Prophet (ﷺ), it is narrated: "Whoever recites ﴿Alif Lam Mim, the revelation of the Book﴾ and ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾, he will be given a reward as if he had brought the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) to life."

And from him (ﷺ), it is narrated: "Whoever recites ﴿Alif Lam Mim, the revelation of the Book﴾ in his house, Satan will not enter his house for three days."
